methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $50M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $1.8B.

data.narrative:
Isembard is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $50M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of nine private robotics firms and one public comparable (ticker: 277810.KQ), including peers such as Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics across seed to Series B stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $50M total raised as a proxy for post-money valuation and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, implies a valuation of $100M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables (Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B, Dexterity at $1.6B, and Walden Robotics at $1.1B) yields a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range of $1.1B to $1.8B.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $85M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $875M. The wide dispersion between stage-progression and peer-median methods reflects material uncertainty in early-stage robotics valuation. Stage-progression is conservative, anchored to capital deployed; peer-median reflects current market pricing for the sector but may incorporate stage premium or market-specific momentum that may not apply to Isembard's specific risk profile. Key uncertainties include the comparability of peer companies' revenue, unit economics, and time-to-scale, as well as the degree to which peer valuations reflect founder-specific versus sector-wide premiums.
